findings.title: getForLogin can return IDPs with isEnabled()==false when their organization is disabled
findings.body: The cached getForLogin resolves IDP IDs via getById, which wraps them with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. This wrapper's isEnabled() returns false if the IDP's organization is disabled. However, the getForLogin method returns these models without filtering by isEnabled(), unlike the delegate implementation which filters at the DB level (ENABLED=true). This means the Infinispan getForLogin can return IDPs that are not actually available for login. The PR adds isEnabled() re-checks in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean to compensate, but any other caller of getForLogin that trusts the method's documented contract ('Returns all identity providers available for login') would receive disabled IDPs. Consider filtering by isEnabled() before returning, or invalidating the login cache when an organization's enabled status changes.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation does not invalidate when a non-login IDP is removed but was previously cached in a login query due to a prior state
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation only invalidates if getLoginPredicate().test(idp) returns true for the removed IDP. However, consider this sequence: (1) IDP is enabled and has no org → it's cached in the login list; (2) IDP is updated to be disabled → registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate correctly invalidates; (3) IDP is updated to be re-enabled but with hideOnLogin=true → predicate fails, no invalidation (correct, it's not a login IDP); (4) IDP is removed → registerIDPLoginInvalidation checks the predicate on the removed model (hideOnLogin=true), predicate fails, no invalidation. This is actually correct because the IDP was already removed from the login cache in step 2. However, if between step 2 and step 4 a cache miss repopulates the login cache (which wouldn't include this IDP since it's hidden), the remove correctly doesn't invalidate. So this is actually fine on deeper analysis, but the logic is fragile and relies on the predicate being evaluated against the current state rather than the cached state.

findings.title: Test cleanup references wrong alias, IDPs created in test won't be cleaned up
findings.body: The cleanup registration uses the literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias (e.g., "idp-alias-" + i): getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove). This means the 20 IDPs created in testCacheIDPForLogin won't be properly cleaned up after the test, potentially affecting other tests. The same issue exists in testCacheIDPByOrg (pre-existing). The cleanup should reference the actual alias, e.g., final String aliasCopy = alias; getCleanup().addCleanup(() -> testRealm().identityProviders().get(aliasCopy).remove()).

findings.title: getForLogin always resolves each cached ID via getById, causing N individual cache lookups
findings.body: The getForLogin method iterates over the cached set of IDs and calls session.identityProviders().getById(id) for each one. While getById itself uses caching, this results in N individual cache lookups plus N potential organization lookups (inside createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel's isEnabled() override) per getForLogin call. For realms with many identity providers, this could be a performance concern on the login page. The existing getByOrganization method has the same pattern, so this is consistent, but worth noting as a potential optimization opportunity (e.g., batch resolution or caching the resolved models).
